title: Constrained node-label permutation null for prior-only spectral-subspace persistence

target_design.cutoff_rule: For target i, construct current and previous leading k=2 pair-residual eigenspaces from strict prefixes draws[:i] and draws[:i-1]. Freeze both subspaces and all overlap values before reading target quintet.

hypothesis: Observed consecutive leading k=2 overlap exceeds a constrained node-label permutation null, and prior-only overlap positively predicts the per-target Top20 hit advantage of frozen Q93 k=2 over Equal42.

permutation_null.transformation: For each fixed node permutation p, transform previous basis as V_previous[p, :]. This preserves orthonormality and the all-ones-orthogonal subspace while disrupting original node-label correspondence.
permutation_null.classification: Constrained node-label permutation null, not a Haar-random subspace null or universal graph null.

association.predictor: Observed prior-only normalized squared Frobenius overlap of consecutive leading k=2 subspaces.
association.outcome: Per-target Top20 hits of frozen Q93::SPECTRAL_K2 minus frozen BASE::EQUAL42.
association.null: Circularly shift the per-target outcome within each chronological split, preserving its serial sequence; inferential only and never a forecast input.
association.split_rule: Use all 640 nonzero offsets in Validation and historical Blind OOS; sample 999 unique nonzero offsets in Discovery.

statistics.bootstrap: Circular moving-block bootstrap, block length 20, 2,000 replicates; report 95% percentile intervals for mean observed-minus-permutation overlap and Spearman rho.
statistics.permutation_p: Within each split, compare observed mean overlap with 999 null means generated by applying each fixed node permutation consistently across targets; plus-one one-sided p-value.
statistics.association_p: Within each split, compare absolute observed Spearman rho with circular-shift null; plus-one two-sided p-value.
statistics.multiple_testing: One global Holm family of six tests: three split-level constrained permutation tests and three split-level circular-shift association tests.
statistics.primary_gate: Both Validation and historical Blind OOS must show positive excess overlap with strictly positive block-bootstrap 95% CI and global Holm p<0.05, and positive Spearman association with strictly positive block-bootstrap 95% CI and global Holm p<0.05. Otherwise NOT_SUPPORTED.

statistical_design_amendment.reason: With six tests in one global Holm family, 99 permutations give a minimum attainable adjusted p-value of 0.06, making alpha=0.05 unattainable. Increase to 999 before outcome analysis; retain seed and constrained transformation.

safeguards: Verify Q93 and Q94 accepted manifests, validation files and source hashes before use.
Current and previous subspaces are recomputed using strict prefixes only.
Permutation transformations are inferential only and never enter forecasts.
Target quintets are read only after prior-only overlap calculations are complete.
Q93 and Equal42 rankings are frozen prior-only forecasts; target outcomes are used only for post-forecast hit accounting.
One global Holm correction covers all six inferential tests.
Historical Blind OOS is exploratory, not virgin prospective confirmation.
No immutable freeze modification, no prospective shadow insertion, no model promotion and no automatic merge.
known_limitations: Node-label permutations are a constrained null, not Haar rotations or a universal graph null.
Subspace overlap is geometric and does not imply causal transfer.
Outcome association is post-forecast and cannot establish causality.
Failure to reject the null does not prove absence of every possible temporal graph structure.
Q60 prospective promotion still requires at least 200 complete paired targets; last persisted count was 21.
next_action: Run strict-prior Q95 and independent replay; append-only persist the full per-target permutation ledger, report, manifest, checkpoint and validation; verify exact Git readback and persisted-head read-only replay. No promotion, merge or freeze changes.
